1930295836425978194 [2025-06-04] @cremieuxrecueil 💜 74 🔁 9 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
PSA:

There are lots of social media influencers who claim to find evidence that everyday products are contaminated with lead and other toxicants by using low-quality tests that generate false-positives.

They alarm consumers by reporting something where nothing is possible. https://t.co/XYsLUdd7yI
Images:
  - [Image #0] The image shows a Reddit post and its corresponding comments. The post is titled "Lead safe mama - is it legit?" and discusses a social media influencer who claims to find lead in everyday products using low-quality tests. 
    
    The post's text is as follows:
    
    "In my local Mom's group someone shared this link about Cupkins having unsafe lead in them and to stop use immediately. I have two of these and my daughter drinks out of them pretty much once or twice a day.
    
    I actually found myself on Lead Safe Mama's page recently about the kitchenaid mixer attachments and now I'm wondering - is her content 100% legit and fact checked or just a passionate mom with a lead-checker machine (or w/e you call it). I can't easily find any of her background information on her website and the fact that she has a shop makes me feel even ickier about her content.
    
    Also god damn it now I have to worry about lead all the time now!"
    
    The first comment is from a user named "aggyface" and reads:
    
    "Okay, so I actually work in a lab and have worked with a variety of x-ray techniques on actual multi-million dollar equipment. I'm also a trained XRF operator and literally do this for a living as well as teach (not for product testing, different industry).
    
    She uses extremely inflammatory language (as you would expect), and seeing her pictures of her using the thing I'm not terribly impressed with her technique (though that's partially that the USA has terrible standards). The certificate she has is from the company itself, not a federal body. (Literally anyone off the street can pay for a one-day training course.) She doesn't really follow ALARA, I don't see a dosimeter or anything, and just...yeah. She argues she's the only one who can do non-biased testing because everyone else is in industry's or government's pockets? I'm not, I work at a university and let me tell you, no one is giving me money for shit, lol. Testing labs aren't all nefarious entities. If you're so concerned, go to an actual testing lab. I believe she does do so on occasion, but carrying an XRF gun like a vigilante through Home Depot? Yikes on bikes.
    
    I've even done knitting needles for kicks and they came up with a lead signal. I put them into my microscope with far, far better resolution and sensitivity (because XRFs honestly kind of suck) and there's nothing there. The instrument and software aren't perfect and there's uncertainties and error she doesn't

It seems like the idea behind some of these accounts is 'pay me or I'll show fake evidence that your product contains lead.' If you're concerned, seek out real testing, not abusive reporting of low-quality tests.
